results.locationRemarks: A fine huge fish trap zigzagged across the entire river here on the shoals which were located about 100 yards above Curry Island. On 1 Sept 1963 this station was collected from the Taladega County side. The stream was quite low. I was unable to reach the station again at low water on the first date, contractors for the Logan Martin Dam were just starting to cut timber off Curry Island. An old private ferry was being used to hand equipment from the Taladega shore to curry Island. Bottom gravel, sand with mussels common in sheltered areas below the Fish Trap Logs. However, most of these had been removed and their animals eaten by muskrats. The river was somewhat deeper on the St Clair county side where the fishtrap reached the shore. Elongated, as usually typical of the forms from large streams. This species [Pleurocera prasinatum] may be found at the stream fringe in silt or mud. These specimens [Anculosa ampla] were taken mostly from the heavy rocks that hold the fish trap logs in place. Here the water flowed Swift, especially when the water was a little higher than when we collected here on September 1st. This fishtrap is shown on a 15 minute US Geological Survey Topographic Map - Taladega 1946. [Changed air mileage from 1.2 to 2.35 and SW to SSW; Quad and coordinates added 29 Jan 2009, ACF].
